judged_text: When sharing is enabled, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips every field except `access_token` (the computed `[z.string().toString()]` keys collapse to a single literal non-matching key), so `data.refresh_token` is always undefined and the code overwrites the credential's real refresh token with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which callers then persist via `prisma.credential.update`. The first token refresh under sharing mode irreversibly replaces stored refresh tokens with the placeholder for providers whose refresh path goes through parse (office365, zoom, webex, lark, zoho). If the sync endpoint is ever unreachable, the feature is disabled, or the deployment falls back to direct refresh, every affected credential is dead and users must re-authenticate — a destructive, one-way write performed automatically on the normal refresh path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` with a `minimumTokenResponseSchema` that uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which in JS/Zod collapses to a single literal property key rather than “any string key”. This means the schema will not properly retain/accept provider fields (including `refresh_token`), and because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, `refresh_token` will be absent from `refreshTokenResponse.data`. The function then unconditionally fills it with the literal string `"refresh_token"` when missing. Call sites such as `Office365CalendarService` spread `tokenResponse.data` back into the stored credential and persist via `prisma.credential.update`, so the refresh token can be clobbered under sharing mode. Regardless, the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` as written is itself invalid for the intended purpose and will likely break refresh parsing under sharing mode.
